title: Certificates of Deposit: deciding whether the payout account named by a maturity payout has been closed
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Certificates of Deposit certificate whose Maturity Instruction pays the balance out to a PCB account when the grace period ends. It decides whether the payout account named on the certificate has been closed.

## Rule

1. Only a Maturity Instruction of **Pay Out to Checking** or **Pay Out to Savings** is concerned. A Maturity Instruction of automatic renewal or of a mailed official check names no account for the maturity payout, so no closure question arises under this rule.
2. Whether the payout account has been closed is read from the status of the account named as the certificate's payout account, in the bank's records:
   - for Pay Out to Savings, the status of that savings account;
   - for Pay Out to Checking, the status of that checking account.
3. A status of closed means the account has been closed. Any other status means it has not.

## Input, judgement, output

| Maturity Instruction | Account whose status is read | Status read | Payout account closed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pay Out to Savings | The savings account named as payout account | Closed | Yes |
| Pay Out to Savings | The savings account named as payout account | Active | No |
| Pay Out to Checking | The checking account named as payout account | Closed | Yes |
| Pay Out to Checking | The checking account named as payout account | Active | No |
| Automatic renewal or mailed official check | None | Not read | Not concerned |

## Points of judgement

**The customer says the account is still in use. Which prevails?**
The status on the bank's record of the named account. A status of closed means it has been closed.

**The certificate pays out to savings, and the owner's checking account is closed. Does that matter here?**
No. For Pay Out to Savings only the status of the named savings account is read.
